bodies: United Motor Works latest coup is a single tender award for the supply. of 102 units 3 ton diesel driven forklift trucks and ten units 2’ ton battery forklifts to PSA. These forklifts are now operating
at PSA’s new gateway at Pasir Panjang, Singapore. Quite apart from this deal Toyota forklift trucks are currently the largest selling range of material handling equipment in Singapore and Malaysia.

Their range of forklifts available covers 1000 kg to 25000 kg diesel driven forklift trucks, petrol and LP. gas trucks from 700 kg to 6000 kg and battery powered from 500 kg to 4000 kg. The main models are available almost immediately. Forklift trucks have made material handling fast, efficient and indeed safe. With international trade growing and material handling becomingmore than just efficient and neat stacking, forklifts have undergone many innovations in adaptability.

The Toyota forklifts come with many attachments suitable for various diversified industries. For very high lifts a 3-stage mast can be fitted to reach a height of 6500 mm (256”). To load and unload in low holds of ships and containers a 2stage full free lift mast can be attached together with a side-shifter. Their forklifts can also be attached with clamps for work with bales of cotton or pulp, drums and a full 360 rotating clamp for paper rolls. Further versatility of these workhorses is obtained by attaching a ram for coiled goods, a crane arm for lifting objects with slings, hinged forks which can be coupled with bucket, load stabilizers for high stack and fragile cargo. Toyota forklifts come with UMW after sales service guarantee. UMW maintain a large fleet of mobile inspection and service vehicles manned by highly skilled trouble-shooter mechanics. This unit minimises lay down time and regularly inspects Toyota forklifts at worksites to diagnose potential problems free of charge, advise on necessary replacement parts and service the trucks if required. They are on call as well. One UMW spokesman added, “Our motto is — service with expertise.” A mouthful? No, a varifiable fact.

8bdeda19-db38-4a93-9b64-4d5e56b09f62.title: CONTAINERISED PLEASURE BOATS
bodies: Newly-built pleasure boats are becoming a common sight on the decks of containerships these days, as the box carriers are proving a safer and faster mode of transport for high-value cargoes. With the systematic loading and unloading and placement of containers on board, uncontainerisable deck cargoes are not so prone to hard knocks that are common in conventional shipping. American Marine, builder of the Grand Banks range of luxury crafts, over the weekend exported a 32 foot model to a client in Europe. The boat was fixed with a cradle and loaded on board the ScanDutch containership Nedlloyd Delft for a slightly over 20-day trip to Denmark. American Marine, which exports about 10 per cent of its boats to Europe, uses containership transport to ensure the high quality finishing of its crafts remains intact when delivered to customers.

bodies: At the East Lagoon on the northern side of the PSA container terminal , two new container berths are now under construction. These berths will cater increased container traffic expected in the next few years. The first berth will provide a special shore based ramp designed to service the three new vessels of the ANRO Consortium which comprises the Australian National Line, Neptune Orient Lines of Singapore, Australia Straits Container Line and Nedllyod Lines. Completion of the berth is expected by the end of September 1977.

The two berths totalling about S$66 million will be 640 metres in length with two main access bridges linking them to a 19.5 hectare marshalling yard and 10.5 heotares of back up land. The schedule was 18 months for completion of the first berth and 26 months for the complete project. To date the schedule has been maintained. Although the extra capacity provided by the 2 berths will help equip the terminal to cater for the estimated growth in container traffic between now and 1980, the project has been designed to be as flexible as possible. Four 35 tonne portainer cranes purchased at a cost of about $$2.56 million each, plus several transtainer cranes will service the berths. This equipment combined with the modern gear and design of the vessels will help cater for the growth in cargo traffic by improving turn-around times and collection and delivery of cargo. The two new berths will be equipped and fully operational by 1979 just about the same time the existing facilities will have reached their optimum capacity. The construction of the two new berths coincides with the commencement of work on a $$50 million inland container depot at Bukit Timah, about 25 kilometres from the terminal. Its function will be a container storage area and a break bulk consolidation depot.

bodies: A RELIABLE and economic method of on-stream analysis for increasing the efficiency of mineral processing is offered by the Australian Mineral Development Laboratories (AMDEL). AMDEL is a contract research organisation providing technical development and consulting services to industry and government in the fields of mineral and material sciences. ‘The on-stream analytical system, using radioisotope immersion probes, has application to heavy metal processing for elements above titanium in the Periodic Table, in larger-scale modern plant. It provides a method of-continuous automatic readout of metal values in process slurry streams, enabling the most efficient operation of mineral processing plant. The highly significant break-through in this new method of analysis has been the Australian development of a range of immersible probes, each housing a detector head assembly, a scintillation counter and a radioisotope source . The probes are designed to measure mineral content and slurry density, with an accuracy practical to the application, using both X-ray fluorescence and X-ray gammaray absorption techniques, while actually immersed in the Process streams. _ The probes aré inexpensive, of rugged construction and easy to install and to replace. Components of the on-stream analytical system are designed and manufactured by AMDEL will research and development support from the Australian Atomic Energy Commission. The Australian Mineral Industry Research Association and the Zinc Corporation. Under the terms of a worldwide agreement, AMDEL carries out the necessary feasibility studies, and designs, manufactures and installs the equipment. The system is sufficiently flexible to allow step-bystep growth from a basic analysis arrangement to one involving fully computerised plant control with feedback from a number of points in the process. Because of this flexibility, the cost of the installation can be effectively controlled to suit the size of the plant. The cost of the equipment, although a half to a third that of competitors, is likely to be about $A113,000 fora typical 3-stream installation. The IOSA immersion probe system has now a proved history of operation for more than five years in Australia and abroad, for copper, lead, zinc, nickel and tin. AMDEL’s services and facilities include: Analytical chemistry, mineralogy, petrology, geochemistry, geochronology, materials technology, ‘operations research, computer services, geostatistics, mine planning, mineral engineering, chemical metallugry, instrumentation, water treatment, process development, feasibility studies, pat design and commissioning. bodies: ASEA, the Swedish worldwide manufacturer of electrical and mechanical equipment, is working on the development of a process using hot isostatic pressing for the safe containment and storage of nuclear waste. This development work which is being carried out at the Company’s High-Pressure Laboratory at Robertsfors, in the north of Sweden, promises to contain all dangers in the disposal of nuclear waste. Under high pressure the waste is compacted together to form a dense and solid body which is harder than any kind of rock including granite! this process which is called hot isostatic pressing, is already been used in some of ASEA’s products, for instance, the Quintus Presses marketed throughout the world including Singapore. This new method will not only interest countries who are now grappling with the nuclear waste problem, but also others like the Republic who are seriously considering nuclear energy as an alternative power to oil. ASEA has been working in the field of highpressure research since the 1940s and has developed a number of processes and products which have led to important breakthroughts in materials technology.

At the East Lagoon on the northern side of the PSA container terminal , two new container berths are now under construction. These berths will cater increased container traffic expected in the next few years. The two berths totalling about S$66 million will be 640 metres in length with two main access bridges linking them to a 19.5 hectare marshalling yard and 10.5 heotares of back up land. The schedule was 18 months for completion of the first berth and 26 months for the complete project. To date the schedule has been maintained. Although the extra capacity provided by the 2 berths will help equip the terminal to cater for the estimated growth in container traffic between now and 1980, the project has been designed to be as flexible as possible. Four 35 tonne portainer cranes purchased at a cost of about $$2.56 million each, plus several transtainer cranes will service the berths. This equipment combined with the modern gear and design of the vessels will help cater for the growth in cargo traffic by improving turn-around times and collection and delivery of cargo. The two new berths will be equipped and fully operational by 1979 just about the same time the existing facilities will have reached their optimum capacity. The construction of the two new berths coincides with the commencement of work on a $$50 million inland container depot at Bukit Timah, about 25 kilometres from the terminal. Its function will be a container storage area and a break bulk consolidation depot.
